instruction: Enable automatic spell checking in LibreOffice Writer for all documents

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling automatic spell checking in LibreOffice Writer. The evaluator checks the LibreOffice configuration file to verify that IsSpellAuto setting under SpellChecking is set to 'true'. Similar difficulty to original task as both involve changing LibreOffice preferences.

llm_judge_reasons: Expected parameter handling is CORRECT (lines 15-18 of metric): When expected.type='rule', framework calls get_rule() which returns config['rules'] directly, so expected IS {'enabled': 'true'}. The code correctly accesses: expected_value = str(expected.get('enabled', '')).lower()
Result parameter handling is CORRECT (line 21): config_file_path = result correctly receives the vm_file path from get_vm_file getter (file.py:74-143)

XML parsing logic is semantically CORRECT (lines 33-43): Properly searches for IsSpellAuto setting under /org.openoffice.Office.Linguistic/SpellChecking path with correct namespace handling. Uses ET.parse() to read the registrymodifications.xcu configuration file
Coverage is COMPLETE: Single requirement instruction (enable auto spell check) is fully verified by checking IsSpellAuto=='true' in the persistent LibreOffice configuration
Postconfig is APPROPRIATE: Closes and reopens document to verify setting persistence globally 'for all documents', not just temporary session state

State accessibility is CORRECT: The vm_file getter retrieves the persistent LibreOffice config file at /home/user/.config/libreoffice/4/user/registrymodifications.xcu which contains the IsSpellAuto setting
Error handling is ROBUST: Includes checks for missing file (line 27-29), XML parsing errors (line 48-50), and missing settings (line 46-47) with appropriate logging
Static validation warnings about vm_file consumption are FALSE POSITIVES - the metric correctly uses result as config_file_path (line 21), checks existence (line 27), and parses XML (line 33)
validation.fix_description: Added explicit os.path.exists() check to make file path operations more detectable by rule-based validator. This addresses the false positive warnings while maintaining correct logic.
